FINAL CLAIM AUDIT
====================================================================================================
Each claim is classified as directly demonstrated, supported but limited, or not demonstrated.

Claim                                                          Status                   Qualification
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Joint adaptation of concurrency and chunk size is novel        not demonstrated         broad joint adaptation is established prior work
LinUCB learns an optimal concurrency policy                    not demonstrated         no optimality or convergence shown
Periodic exploration breaks frozen-arm starvation              directly demonstrated    coverage only; not preference change
Periodic exploration causes posterior adaptation               directly demonstrated    boundary/forced events; deterministic not learned
Periodic exploration causes effective controller changes       directly demonstrated    scenario-dependent; deterministic exploration
LinUCB consistently improves performance                       not demonstrated         descriptive only; no superiority claim
Chunk-size adaptation is successfully learned                  not demonstrated         unmodelled tradeoff; not evidence of optimization
The internal downloader outperforms aria2                      not demonstrated         descriptive; granularity/connection differences remain
aria2 is inferior under consumer networks                      not demonstrated         no real-network deployment
Request granularity explains a substantial portion of the original aria2 difference supported but limited    residual ~74 ms unexplained
Wall-clock throttling removes the request-count confound       supported but limited    removes the trigger coupling for all granularities; does not equalize downloaders
The controller generalizes to real consumer networks           not demonstrated         no external validity established
The method is fair to competing downloaders                    not demonstrated         fairness explicitly absent
The system demonstrates RL-based adaptation                    not demonstrated         adaptation observed with deterministic periodic exploration, not learned exploration
The current evidence establishes causal action effectiveness   not demonstrated         temporal attribution approximate

SUPPORTED CONCLUSIONS (directly demonstrated):
  - Periodic exploration breaks frozen-arm starvation
  - Periodic exploration causes posterior adaptation
  - Periodic exploration causes effective controller changes

SUPPORTED BUT LIMITED:
  - Request granularity explains a substantial portion of the original aria2 difference -- residual ~74 ms unexplained
  - Wall-clock throttling removes the request-count confound -- removes the trigger coupling for all granularities; does not equalize downloaders

NOT SUPPORTED BY CURRENT EVIDENCE:
  - Joint adaptation of concurrency and chunk size is novel -- broad joint adaptation is established prior work
  - LinUCB learns an optimal concurrency policy -- no optimality or convergence shown
  - LinUCB consistently improves performance -- descriptive only; no superiority claim
  - Chunk-size adaptation is successfully learned -- unmodelled tradeoff; not evidence of optimization
  - The internal downloader outperforms aria2 -- descriptive; granularity/connection differences remain
  - aria2 is inferior under consumer networks -- no real-network deployment
  - The controller generalizes to real consumer networks -- no external validity established
  - The method is fair to competing downloaders -- fairness explicitly absent
  - The system demonstrates RL-based adaptation -- adaptation observed with deterministic periodic exploration, not learned exploration
  - The current evidence establishes causal action effectiveness -- temporal attribution approximate
